top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) recognises design-based local-labour-market evidence that adjustment to import competition was slow, concentrated and persistent, a first-order question that overturned the prior that workers and regions reallocate quickly. The core papers are over a decade old and have been tested through critiques of shift-share identification, exposure measurement and persistence, which refined magnitudes without reversing the central finding. Attribution is the tightest on the slate because the empirical programme is jointly authored by the three, and a citation limited to exposure, local adjustment and persistence avoids claiming an effect size or the origins of the task framework. Reservations remain: Katz and the task lineage are uncredited, long-run magnitudes are contested, and the 2021, 2023 and 2024 prizes are thematically adjacent. I do not treat the ten-member support count as evidence of merit. P002 (Helpman, Melitz) is a mature, cleanly framed mechanism, but its priority questions (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum) and its overlap with the 2008 prize are unresolved, so I rank it second. Both are preferable to no award.
recusal_note: No tie to Autor, Dorn or Hanson, or to Helpman or Melitz, is apparent from my profile. I am a frequent co-author of Per Krusell (secretary) and have co-authored with Timo Boppart and Richard Friberg, who both support P001 or are adjacent to P002. I am an IIES colleague of Krusell and Boppart. These are collegial ties, not ties to candidates. I gave the 2018 and 2025 speeches on adjacent growth prizes, which do not establish private preferences. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
